Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

technical adjective

belonging to a particular art, trade or science

also technical term, technical terms, technical language, technically

our formation

Cic. N.D. 2.57: Zēnō cēnset artis proprium esse creāre et gignere (Lewis & Short)

artis proprius, propria, proprium

proper to an art, technical

Latin says what belongs to an art with the genitive artis or the name of the field: a technical term is vocābulum artis proprium, or one of the field (mīlitāre vocābulum, Tac. Ann. 1.41). The phrase is ours, made after Cicero’s artis proprium.

Other words

  • artificiālis, artificiāle — according to the rules of an art

    also used · post-classical · Quint. 5.1.1: probātiōnēs (Lewis & Short)

    Only in Quintilian (Lewis & Short), of the proofs the orator makes by his art, as against those he finds.

  • technicus, technicī m. — a teacher of an art (not an adjective)

    noun, second declension · avoid · post-classical · Quint. 2.13.15 (Lewis & Short)

    In Latin a noun, “a teacher of an art” (Lewis & Short), Quintilian’s word for the writers on the art of rhetoric; it does not mean “technical”.

Examples

  • quem mīlitārī vocābulō Caligulam appellābant

    whom they called Caligula, in the soldiers’ wordTac. Ann. 1.41

See also technology, technique, skill.
